questions.prompt: Do you have a favorite teacher?

answers.basic: One of my favourite teachers was my secondary school maths teacher. They were good at showing how to get started when a problem looked too hard. I remember them starting with a smaller example, which often made it clear why the same idea worked in the bigger question.

questions.prompt: Do you want to be a teacher in the future?

answers.basic: I already teach badminton part-time, and I enjoy it. I'd like to keep coaching alongside my work as a software engineer. I get a lot out of seeing someone understand a movement, like when a student suddenly finds a more comfortable grip.

questions.prompt: Do you have a teacher from your past that you still remember?

answers.basic: Yes, I still remember my maths teacher. They used to ask how I got an answer, which made me pay more attention to the steps. One thing that stuck with me was having to explain a shortcut to the class, because it made me see what I'd missed.

questions.prompt: Are you still in touch with your primary school teachers?

answers.basic: No, I've lost touch with them over the years. I still remember a few things they used to say in class. We moved on to different schools, so there wasn't much chance to see them again except when I happened to pass the old building.

questions.prompt: In what way has your favourite teacher helped you?

answers.basic: My maths teacher showed me how to break a big question into smaller ones. I use that habit when I'm stuck on a problem at work now. If a service is slow, for instance, I'll check one request step by step instead of trying to fix everything at once.

questions.prompt: Do you like your primary school teachers more than your high school teachers?

answers.basic: I remember my high school teachers more clearly because I was old enough to ask them questions about what to do next. I have good memories of primary school too. A high school teacher might talk through a choice of subjects with me, which felt useful because it affected what I could study later.
